derivations.claim:
In polar coordinates $(r,\theta)$ write the smooth one-form
$\widetilde A=\widetilde A_r\,dr+\widetilde A_\theta\,d\theta$.
For a disk of radius $R$, integration of
$\widetilde F_{r\theta}=\partial_r\widetilde A_\theta-
\partial_\theta\widetilde A_r$ first in $r$ and then in $\theta$ gives
$\int_{|x|\le R}\widetilde F_{12}\,d^2x
=\int_0^{2\pi}\widetilde A_\theta(R,\theta)\,d\theta$: the
$\theta$-derivative term cancels by single-valuedness, and the inner
boundary term tends to zero because a smooth one-form has
$\widetilde A_\theta=O(r)$ at the origin.

On a sufficiently large circle choose a continuous phase
$M/|M|=e^{i\vartheta(\theta)}$ with
$\vartheta(2\pi)-\vartheta(0)=2\pi n$. The tangential condition in [F1]
implies $\widetilde A_\theta(R,\theta)-
\partial_\theta\vartheta(\theta)\to0$ uniformly in $\theta$ as
$R\to\infty$.
Taking the limit in step 1.1 therefore gives
$\Phi_D=\int_0^{2\pi}\partial_\theta\vartheta\,d\theta=2\pi n$.

Since $n\ne0$, step 2.1 gives nonzero flux, so the smooth function
$\widetilde F_{12}$ is nonzero at some point and hence on a neighborhood of
that point. Its squared integral is strictly positive. By [F2] and
$g_D>0$, the Maxwell term contributes strictly positive energy, while all
remaining energy terms are nonnegative; thus $\sigma>0$. Finiteness of
$\sigma$ is part of [F1]'s admitted-profile hypothesis.

derivations.claim:
The current model carrier [A1] fixes the $SU(2)$ gauge and coupling
conventions but includes one hypermultiplet, so it does not supply the
no-matter assumption in [A2]. We retain that pure-model input separately and
condition this calculation on the exact local effective data [F1].
Differentiating its superpotential gives
$\partial_{A_D}W_\mu=\sqrt2M\widetilde M+\mu u'(A_D)$,
$\partial_MW_\mu=\sqrt2A_D\widetilde M$, and
$\partial_{\widetilde M}W_\mu=\sqrt2A_DM$. By [F2], a supersymmetric
vacuum in this canonical model must set all three derivatives and
$D=g_D(|M|^2-|\widetilde M|^2)$ equal to zero.

If $A_D\ne0$, the second and third equations in step 1.1 force
$M=\widetilde M=0$, after which the first equation is
$\mu u'(A_D)=0$, contradicting $\mu\ne0$ and the nonvanishing derivative
on the patch. Hence $A_D=0$. The first equation then gives
$M\widetilde M=-\mu c/\sqrt2\ne0$, so both fields are nonzero.

The D equation in step 1.1 and $g_D>0$ give
$|M|=|\widetilde M|=:v$. Taking absolute values in the product equation
from step 2.1 yields $v^2=|\mu c|/\sqrt2$, so
$v=(|\mu c|/\sqrt2)^{1/2}>0$.

Given any solution of these equations, choose a $U(1)_D$ phase so that
$M=v$ is positive real. The product equation then uniquely fixes
$\widetilde M=-\mu c/(\sqrt2v)$. Thus every solution is gauge-equivalent
to this representative, proving uniqueness of the vacuum orbit in the
chosen patch.

Since $M\ne0$, a gauge transformation that fixes the representative
must satisfy $e^{i\alpha}M=M$, hence $e^{i\alpha}=1$. The stabilizer is
trivial, so $U(1)_D$ is fully Higgsed.

Write $\widetilde A_{c,\mu}=\widetilde A_\mu/g_D$ for the canonically
normalized gauge field. Expanding the scalar kinetic terms from [F1] around
the constant representative gives the quadratic vector term
$-g_D^2(|M|^2+|\widetilde M|^2)
\widetilde A_{c,\mu}\widetilde A_c^{\mu}$. Comparing with the Proca
normalization $-m_D^2\widetilde A_{c,\mu}\widetilde A_c^{\mu}/2$
gives $m_D^2=2g_D^2(|M|^2+|\widetilde M|^2)=4g_D^2v^2>0$.

Under the additional vortex/minimization hypothesis in the Statement,
[F4] gives nonzero quantized original electric flux and a tension
$\sigma>0$. The interior of a translation-invariant tube of length $L$
contains the same transverse profile at each longitudinal coordinate, so
its bulk energy is $\sigma L$. The uniformly bounded endcap contribution
therefore gives $V(L)=\sigma L+O(1)$, which is linear confinement in this
effective model. This last conclusion is conditional: no preceding step
establishes existence or minimization of the required profile.

citations.quote: A **classical supersymmetric vacuum configuration** is a constant scalar

derivations.claim:
Since $W=0$, both holomorphic derivatives vanish identically, so every
$(q,\widetilde q)$ is F-flat. The D equation is
$-g(|q|^2-|\widetilde q|^2)=0$; because $g>0$, it is equivalent to
$|q|=|\widetilde q|$. By [F1], the classical vacuum set is exactly that
D-flat set modulo the displayed U(1) action.

The product $m=q\widetilde q$ is invariant under the action, since
$(e^{i\alpha}q)(e^{-i\alpha}\widetilde q)=q\widetilde q$. It therefore
defines a map from the D-flat orbit set to $\mathbb C$.

For any $m_0\in\mathbb C$ with $m_0\ne0$, choose
$q=\sqrt{|m_0|}>0$ and $\widetilde q=m_0/q$. Then
$q\widetilde q=m_0$ and $|q|=|\widetilde q|=\sqrt{|m_0|}$; for
$m_0=0$, choose $(q,\widetilde q)=(0,0)$. Thus every $m_0$ is attained by
a D-flat pair.

If two D-flat pairs have the same product $m_0=0$, their equal-modulus
condition forces both pairs to be $(0,0)$. If $m_0\ne0$, both $q$-entries
are nonzero and have modulus $\sqrt{|m_0|}$; hence their ratio is a phase
$e^{i\alpha}$, and equality of products forces the corresponding
$\widetilde q$-entries to differ by $e^{-i\alpha}$. The two pairs are
therefore U(1)-gauge-equivalent. The map in step 2.1 is injective as well
as surjective, proving the stated bijection.

derivations.claim:
In the electric theory, each of the $N_c$ color components of $Q$ is a
left-handed Weyl fermion in $\mathbf N_f$ of $SU(N_f)_L$, so these fields
contribute $N_c$. The antiquarks and gaugino are $SU(N_f)_L$ singlets and
contribute zero. Hence
$\mathcal A_{\mathrm{electric}}=N_c$.

In the magnetic theory, the $\widetilde N_c$ color copies of $q$ are
antifundamentals and contribute $-\widetilde N_c$. For each of the $N_f$
right-flavor components of $M$, its left-flavor index is fundamental, so
the meson fermions contribute $+N_f$. The magnetic antiquarks and gaugino
are left-flavor singlets. Therefore
$\mathcal A_{\mathrm{magnetic}}=-\widetilde N_c+N_f$.

Substituting $\widetilde N_c=N_f-N_c$ gives
$\mathcal A_{\mathrm{magnetic}}=-(N_f-N_c)+N_f=N_c
=\mathcal A_{\mathrm{electric}}$. This verifies the stated cubic-anomaly
match.

The calculation checks only this specified global-symmetry coefficient
under the proposed field assignments. It supplies no map of all observables,
no equivalence of renormalization-group flows, and no continuum construction;
therefore it does not prove the proposed duality.

derivations.claim:
Differentiating $W_\mu=\sqrt2 A_D M\widetilde M+\mu u(A_D)$ gives
$F_{A_D}=\sqrt2 M\widetilde M+\mu u'(A_D)$,
$F_M=\sqrt2 A_D\widetilde M$, and
$F_{\widetilde M}=\sqrt2 A_DM$. At $A_D=0$, the first equation is
$\sqrt2M\widetilde M+\mu c=0$, while the other two vanish.

Set $v=(|\mu c|/\sqrt2)^{1/2}>0$ and
$\widetilde M=-\mu c/(\sqrt2v)$, with $M=v$. Then
$M\widetilde M=-\mu c/\sqrt2$ and
$|\widetilde M|=|\mu c|/(\sqrt2v)=v$, so all F equations and
$D=g_D(|M|^2-|\widetilde M|^2)=0$ hold.

Any solution in this patch with $A_D\ne0$ would have
$M=\widetilde M=0$ by the last two F equations, contradicting
$\mu u'(A_D)\ne0$ in the first. Thus $A_D=0$; the first F equation fixes
the nonzero product and the D equation fixes equal magnitudes. The U(1)
phase can then make $M=v$ and fixes $\widetilde M$ as in the Example, so
the solution is one gauge orbit.

Expanding the canonical kinetic terms around $M=v$ and
$|\widetilde M|=v$, and canonically normalizing
$\widetilde A_c=\widetilde A/g_D$, gives
$m_D^2=2g_D^2(|M|^2+|\widetilde M|^2)=4g_D^2v^2>0$. This verifies the
local Higgs mass only; it supplies no vortex solution.
